fields.description:
Found in ticket 18a4's Phase-1 investigation.

DEFECT. `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_dc_transport_pagination_heldout.py` carries the
structural guard `test_no_search_issues_call_relies_on_the_default_page_size`, whose stated job
is "THE CRITERION THAT CONVERTS 'I fixed two' INTO 'a fourth cannot be added silently'": it
AST-scans for any `search_issues(...)` call that omits an explicit result cap (which would take
`max_results=50` and silently truncate past 50 issues).

It scans exactly ONE file -- `_TRANSPORT_SRC`, i.e.
`adapters/jira_datacenter/transport.py` (test file line ~31).

Ticket 465d's one-module-per-capability split then moved the pager and every `search_issues`
call OUT of `transport.py` (the pager now lives in `_base.py`; the single-page primitive in
`_issues.py:262`). MEASURED on origin/main at fc705c64410: an AST walk of `transport.py` finds
**0** `search_issues` calls. The guard now scans a file that no longer contains the construct it
polices, so it passes unconditionally and would not notice a fifth unpaginated caller added
anywhere in the DC adapter.

This is a rotted guard, not a missing one -- and pointedly so: its own sibling test's docstring
says "A structural test that cannot fail is decoration -- and this one exists precisely because
the previous audit of this seam under-counted."

PROPOSED FIX: widen the scan from the single `transport.py` path to every `*.py` in
`adapters/jira_datacenter/`, and add a teeth test proving the widened predicate actually reaches
`_base.py` and `_issues.py`. Pre-checked: both current call sites pass an explicit cap
(`_base.py:148` `maxResults=page_size`, `_issues.py:262` `maxResults=max_results`), so widening
should go green immediately -- confirm rather than assume. Consider whether the same rot hit
other single-file AST guards that 465d's split moved code out from.

NOT folded into 18a4 deliberately: 465d owns the module re-architecture whose split caused this,
and the repair changes a pre-existing guard's SCOPE (which can surface unrelated offenders), so
it is its own reviewable unit.

Acceptance criteria:
- [x] The guard scans every module in `adapters/jira_datacenter/`, not just `transport.py`
- [x] A teeth test proves the widened predicate reports a synthetic uncapped call in a
      NON-transport.py module (so it cannot silently rot the same way again)
- [x] Audit and report whether any other single-file AST guard was emptied by 465d's split

---

## PROVEN ROOT CAUSE (Phase 1 confirmed — see RCA comment for the full experiment log)

`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_dc_transport_pagination_heldout.py:31-34` binds
`_TRANSPORT_SRC` to the single hardcoded path
`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_datacenter/transport.py`, and
`_search_issues_calls_taking_the_default()` `ast.parse()`s exactly that one file. Commit
`4213081d23` ("Split DC transport into capability mixins", rebar-ticket 465d) moved both
`search_issues` call sites out of `transport.py` (they were at transport.py:365 and :406
before the split) into `_issues.py` and `_base.py`, and its own message states "Pure text
move: no test edited" — the hardcoded scan path was never moved with the code. Measured at
HEAD: an AST walk of `transport.py` finds **0** `search_issues` call nodes, and the live
predicate returns `[]`, so `assert not offenders` is unconditionally true.

## PLAN (mechanical; test-only, no runtime behaviour change)

1. **Widen the scan.** Replace `_TRANSPORT_SRC` with `_DC_ADAPTER_DIR`
   (`adapters/jira_datacenter/`) and have `_search_issues_calls_taking_the_default()` walk
   every `*.py` in it, reporting offenders as `<module>.py:<line>` so a failure names the
   file. Keep the existing `src=` override parameter so the current teeth test is unaffected.
2. **Add a non-vacuity assertion.** The guard must also assert the widened scan observed a
   NON-ZERO number of `search_issues` call sites. This is the anti-rot repair proper: if a
   future move empties the directory again, the suite goes RED instead of silently disarming.
   Without this, criterion 1 alone leaves the same rot possible one directory up.
3. **Add a teeth test for the widened predicate** proving it reports a synthetic uncapped
   call attributed to a NON-`transport.py` module, so the directory walk (not just the
   string-source path) is exercised.
4. **Audit** the rest of `tests/` for other single-file AST/structural guards emptied by
   465d's split and report the finding on this ticket.

Pre-measured: both live call sites already pass an explicit cap (`_base.py:172`
`maxResults=page_size`; `_issues.py:262` `maxResults=max_results`) and every other module in
the directory has zero calls, so the widened guard goes green immediately. No `src/` file is
modified.

### file_impact (declared)
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_dc_transport_pagination_heldout.py` (the only file changed)

### Verification
- `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_dc_transport_pagination_heldout.py` — full module green
- RED proof: the non-vacuity assertion fails against the current single-file scan before the fix
- Mutation check: re-pin the scan to `transport.py` only -> the non-vacuity test returns RED
- `make lint` + `make typecheck`

### Out of scope / explicitly NOT changed
- The DC pager's behaviour, page-size handling, and offset-stall logic (18a4) are untouched.
- No change to any `src/` module; this ticket only restores a guard's scope.
